overview:
This check monitors [Celery][1] through the Datadog Agent. Celery is a distributed task queue system that enables asynchronous task processing in Python applications.

The Celery integration provides valuable insights into your task queue system by:
- Monitoring worker health, status, and task execution metrics
- Tracking task processing rates, runtime, and prefetch times
- Providing visibility into worker performance and task distribution
- Helping identify bottlenecks and optimize task processing efficiency

**Minimum Agent version:** 7.66.0

[1]: https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/monitoring.html
setup:
Follow the instructions below to install and configure this check for an Agent running on a host. For containerized environments, see the [Autodiscovery Integration Templates][3] for guidance on applying these instructions.

### Installation

The Celery check is included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package.
No additional installation is needed on your server.

### Prerequisites

1. Install and configure [Celery Flower][10], the real-time web monitor and administration tool for [Celery][1].

### Configuration

1. Edit the `celery.d/conf.yaml` file in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your Agent's configuration directory to start collecting your Celery performance data. See the [sample celery.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

    ```yaml
    init_config:

    instances:
      ## @param openmetrics_endpoint - string - required
      ## Endpoint exposing the Celery Flower's Prometheus metrics
      #
      - openmetrics_endpoint: http://localhost:5555/metrics
    ```

2. [Restart the Agent][5].

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][6] and look for `celery` under the Checks section.

metrics.name: celery.flower.events.count
metrics.description: The count of Celery events from the last submission.

metrics.name: celery.flower.events.created
metrics.description: The number of Celery events created.

metrics.name: celery.flower.task.prefetch_time.seconds
metrics.description: Time tasks spend waiting at worker before execution.

metrics.name: celery.flower.task.runtime.seconds.bucket
metrics.description: The number of observations within each distribution bucket of the tasks runtime.

metrics.name: celery.flower.task.runtime.seconds.sum
metrics.description: The total duration of a task runtime.

metrics.name: celery.flower.worker.executing_tasks
metrics.description: Number of tasks currently executing at a worker.

metrics.name: celery.flower.worker.online
metrics.description: Worker online status (1 for online, 0 for offline).

metrics.name: celery.flower.worker.prefetched_tasks
metrics.description: Number of tasks prefetched at a worker.

serviceChecks.name: Celery Flower OpenMetrics endpoint health
serviceChecks.description: Returns `CRITICAL` if the Agent is unable to connect to the Celery OpenMetrics endpoint, otherwise returns `OK`.

monitors.title: Celery workers are idle.
monitors.description: This monitor alerts when the number of tasks currently executing at this worker is 0.

monitors.title: Celery workers are offline.
monitors.description: This monitor alerts when the number of Celery workers online is 0.
